clue.text: Special athletes who possibly get most attention

indicators.note: possibly says the letters before it may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Talented sportspeople naturally hog the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is the idiom for outshining everyone else on stage or at an event.

clue.text: Person serving in battle on ship essentially lost

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the battle above the ship piece

parts.note: the Somme was a major First World War battle

indicators.note: essentially lost means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A wartime sailor at the Somme has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially lost' drops the middle N of LINER, leaving LIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the wine waiter in a restaurant, someone who serves drinks to diners.

clue.text: Hard cutting smooth 22s up to form spiky layers

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sand is to smooth

indicators.note: cutting means the letter slices into the other pieces

parts.note: 22 across is DIAMOND; ice is slang for diamonds
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes polishing gems with something hard to create spiky layers.
explanation.walkthrough: H cuts SANDICE to make SANDIHCE, which 'up' turns over. 'layers' means egg-layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Echidnas are spiny anteaters, among the very few mammals that lay eggs.

clue.text: Painter humble with the second-hand exchange?

indicators.note: a hand is left or right, so the second L, for left, is exchanged for R, for right

parts.note: lowly means humble

explanation.surface: A modest artist has a deal involving used goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-hand exchange' swaps the second L (left hand) of LOWLY for R (right hand).
explanation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry was the English artist famous for his scenes of northern industrial towns.

clue.text: Obstacle course evacuated after deer bolted

indicators.note: after puts the emptied course piece behind the deer and bolted pieces

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
to bolt is to run, past tense ran

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters stay

explanation.surface: An obstacle course is cleared when a deer charges through.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that gets in the way, a synonym of obstacle.

clue.text: Mounting of princess is brown tinged with yellow

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means rising, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A princess's horse is described as yellowish brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting of' reverses ANNEIS. Princess Anne is a well-known equestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment; raw sienna is a yellowish brown colour.

clue.text: Gory bits maybe supplied by Gore

parts.note: to get something off someone is to have it supplied by them
Al Gore was US Vice President

explanation.surface: Bloody meat scraps were handed over by Gore.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore's first name is the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a butchered animal, the bloody leftovers.

clue.text: 13 hands regularly on ruby cushion

parts.note: 13 across is BRIGANTINE; its hands are sailors, ABs (able seamen)

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Sailors take turns resting on a red cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O, R, B from ON RUBY.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb a blow is to cushion it, soaking up the force.

clue.text: Fate of idiot atop house

indicators.note: atop in a down clue puts the idiot above the house piece

parts.note: a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool's destiny lies on top of his home.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who spins the thread of life.

clue.text: Centre admitting Boris sent back a lot of paperwork

indicators.note: sent back says the whole assembled string is read in reverse order
admitting means the first piece lets the second in, holding it inside

parts.note: a hub is a centre
Boris Johnson was PM, Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A government office returns a stack of forms because of Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' gives HPMUB, which 'sent back' reverses; Boris Johnson was Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumph is British slang for tedious, superfluous printed documents and forms.

clue.text: Fund lower after crash: great!

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cheer as an investment fund falls further after a market collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges the letters of FUND LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of delight, so one swaps for the other as a cry of approval.

clue.text: Chance to visit Doris following competition?

indicators.note: following says the second name comes after the first piece in the answer

parts.note: an Open is a competition open to all, as in golf's Open
Doris Day was the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is a chance to drop in on Doris after a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An open day is when an institution such as a school lets the public come and look round.

clue.text: Lock phone before Terry returns

indicators.note: before puts the phone piece ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: returns says the short form of the name is read backwards

parts.note: Tel is a familiar short form of Terry

explanation.surface: Someone must lock up and make a call before Terry gets home.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair can be a curl, which is what a ringlet is.

clue.text: Huge one going last into saltwater vessel

indicators.note: into puts the reworked huge word inside the salt-water word

parts.note: brine is salt water

indicators.note: going last says the letter for one is moved to the end of its word

parts.note: giant means huge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A giant goes last onto a ship on the salty sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going last' makes GANTI, which 'into' places in the salt water word; 'Huge' looks like a description of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Poor 'rithmetic perhaps later discovered

parts.note: the three Rs are reading, 'riting and 'rithmetic, so 'rithmetic is the third R

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover, the outer letters, taken off

explanation.surface: Someone poor at arithmetic finds out later.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of low quality, so it serves as poor in that sense.

clue.text: 22's elemental unit detailed for Roman senator

parts.note: 22 across is DIAMOND, a form of carbon, chemical symbol C

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: an atom is the basic unit of an element

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson on a diamond's basic unit somehow names an ancient politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder and Cato the Younger were statesmen in the Senate of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Revolutionary supports a structured naval barrage

indicators.note: supports in a down clue puts the revolutionary below the other pieces
structured suggests the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary backs a carefully planned bombardment from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming flood of something, just as a barrage is.

clue.text: Player of tennis match beginning to inspire artwork

parts.note: Steffi Graf was a German tennis champion
to fit is to match

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tennis star's game starts to inspire a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is street art painted or scrawled on walls, so it is artwork.

clue.text: Connection out of Dover or Ostend

indicators.note: out of says the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A ferry link runs from Dover or Ostend.
explanation.definitionFit: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry, a vehicle link across a stretch of sea.

clue.text: Edit scenes south of Bordeaux?

indicators.note: south of in a down clue puts the scenes below the wine piece

parts.note: Bordeaux is often a red wine
an act is a series of scenes in a play

explanation.surface: Someone is cutting film footage set in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to edit it, often blacking out sensitive passages.

clue.text: Approximately Robin Hood's dilemma over low earners?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for roughly or approximately

definitions.text: Robin Hood's dilemma over low earners?
definitions.meaning: the outlaw robbed the rich to give to the poor

explanation.definitionFit: Give or take is an idiom attached to a figure to mean roughly, within a small margin.

clue.text: Really upset contingent of Mykonos revellers

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
contingent of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of partygoers on a Greek island are truly distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contingent of' picks OSREVE from Mykonos revellers and 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is a British colloquial intensifier meaning very or truly.

clue.text: Stage when steroid finally is injected into swine

indicators.note: is injected into puts the picked letter inside the animals' word

parts.note: boars are swine

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A doping scandal on a pig farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The boards is a metonym for the stage, as in treading the boards.

clue.text: It's cut not paste

parts.note: paste is imitation gem glass; the real gemstone is cut, and the surface also suggests editing with cut and paste

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a word-processing instruction; the real sense is jewellery, where paste is a fake gem.
explanation.definitionFit: This precious stone is faceted by cutting, and paste is its glass imitation.

clue.text: What might be picked from behind mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word is used, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: astern means behind, on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might be picked from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a garden flower, the sort of thing one picks for a bunch.

clue.text: Collapse of residence into river

indicators.note: into says the home goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England

clue.text: Heads of departments eventually left thank you letter

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Department heads finally left a note of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Surprised at a curlew's cry

indicators.note: surprised suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at the call of a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is a shrill wailing howl, like a cat's, so it is a kind of cry.

clue.text: Tiny bone is inlaid with new copper

indicators.note: inlaid with means the word is has other pieces set inside it

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A small skeletal piece has been decorated with fresh copper.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, or anvil, is one of the three small ossicles in the middle ear.

clue.text: Question angry old tyrant associated with Spain

parts.note: cross means angry
ex means former or old
Idi Amin was the brutal dictator of Uganda
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A furious interrogation of a former Spanish dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross-examine is to interrogate a witness in court, a formal kind of questioning.
